answer: Each identity anchors to a tax-filing history: returns filed year after year, with the tax authority confirming the record. A vine grows one season at a time, and a filing history is the same: it cannot be planted fully grown. A comet appears suddenly and vanishes, and so does a farm's tax record: a single filing, or none at all, where honest agents show a decade. Black as onyx is the record of a filer whose returns stretch back years; the authority's own database is the proof, and a Sybil operator cannot file a past that never happened.
